Two abstract authority activation protocols are compared only for stale-claimant exclusion and crash ordering: P1 independent authoritative monotonic fence activation; P2 quiescent two-phase activation using an authoritative transition state before record CAS and final E1 activation. No concrete transport, public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, hosted compute, richer-mode arbitration, finite quota, or second semantic leaf is modeled.

steps: Atomically advance the authoritative current-fence value from E0 to E1.

After that activation, every effect attempt and every authority-sensitive mutation must validate current_fence == E1 at the operation boundary; E0 is rejected even if the role-local effect record still says E0.
CAS the effect record authority field from E0 to E1 while preserving generation/effect-key/payload-hash/acceptance fields.

crash_replay.before_fence_advance: E0 remains authoritative and E1 must not act; retry may safely repeat the same E0->E1 fence CAS attempt under expected-old validation.
crash_replay.after_fence_advance_before_record_cas: E0 is already invalid. E1 may proceed only through operations that atomically validate the authoritative fence; the lagging record cannot authorize E0.
crash_replay.after_record_cas: Record and current fence both say E1; stale E0 remains rejected.

minimum_durable_state: stable generation/effect identity preserved across claimant turnover
protocols.condition: No cross-record transaction is needed only if the fence primitive is independently authoritative and is checked atomically enough at every side-effect/state-mutation boundary.

steps: Atomically move authority from active(E0) to quiescent(pending E1), making no claimant executable.
While quiescent, CAS the effect record authority field from E0 to E1 while preserving generation/effect-key/payload-hash/acceptance fields.
After durable record CAS, atomically move authority from quiescent(pending E1) to active(E1).

crash_replay.before_quiescence: E0 remains active; E1 must not act.
crash_replay.after_quiescence_before_record_cas: No claimant is active, so stale E0 and premature E1 effects are both rejected; recovery resumes the record CAS.
crash_replay.after_record_cas_before_E1_activation: Record says E1 but authority remains quiescent; no effect runs. Recovery may validate the E1 record then activate E1.
crash_replay.after_E1_activation: Only E1 is active and E0 remains rejected.

minimum_durable_state: one authoritative authority-state record with active/quiescent mode and pending/active epoch
stable generation/effect identity preserved across the transition
protocols.condition: The quiescent authority state must itself be authoritative and every effect attempt must reject while quiescent. This replaces a cross-record atomic transaction with two atomic authority transitions plus one effect-record CAS and explicit crash recovery.

comparison.shared_hard_requirement: An independently authoritative operation-boundary check must invalidate E0 before E1 can execute; consulting only the lagging effect record is insufficient.
comparison.P1_tradeoff: Fewer transitions and higher availability, but requires the side-effect/state surface to validate the current monotonic fence during each protected operation.
comparison.P2_tradeoff: Introduces a safe no-owner interval that makes crash ordering explicit and can simplify reasoning, but adds recovery states and temporary loss of liveness. It still needs an authoritative quiescent/active gate checked by every protected operation.
comparison.atomicity_not_eliminated: Each authority-state transition and each effect-record CAS still needs single-record atomic compare-and-set semantics; the replay does not prove a concrete Chat-exposed primitive providing them.

observations: The unsafe part of crash window A is not record lag by itself; it is permitting stale E0 operations during that lag. Both protocols become safe only when a separate authoritative gate rejects E0 before any E1 effect can occur.

A cross-record atomic transaction is not logically necessary for this modeled safety property. P1 tolerates temporary record lag behind an already-active fence; P2 prevents all effects during record migration through a quiescent authority state.
P2 converts a concurrency-safety problem into a bounded liveness interruption: crashes between quiescence and E1 activation are safe but require replay to finish activation.
Neither protocol establishes a concrete scheduled-Chat implementation because the existence and quota-zero behavior of a Chat-exposed authoritative fence/quiescence primitive remains unverified.
inference: For the exact abstract crash-window-A model, stale-claimant safety can be achieved without an atomic transaction spanning authority and effect records. The minimal design obligation is an independently authoritative gate whose state transition invalidates E0 before E1 can execute. P1 makes E1 active first and tolerates effect-record lag; P2 first enters a durable no-owner state, migrates the effect record, then activates E1. Both preserve the same stable logical effect identity and require only per-record atomic transitions, but both leave the concrete Chat-exposed primitive child unresolved.
unresolved_children: Verify a concrete allowed zero-cost quota-independent Chat-exposed primitive that can serve as the authoritative current-fence or active/quiescent gate and can be checked at each protected operation boundary.
Verify that the same allowed surface supports single-record monotonic CAS/reconstruction under interruption and rate limiting without hosted coordination or manual execution.
Verify end-to-end same-key idempotent effect acceptance after the authority protocol, including acknowledgement-loss replay, on an allowed concrete surface.
